title: M-QUEST - Meme Question-Understanding Evaluation on Semantics and Toxicity
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the ability of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to detect and reason about toxicity in memes using a novel semantic framework. While not primarily focused on faith/religion, the framework measures the models' capabilities to identify hate speech, harmful stereotypes, and toxicity directed at specific target communities, including religious groups (e.g., detecting and reasoning about Islamophobic tropes and Muslim stereotypes in meme images and text).
findings: The paper does not provide aggregate findings specifically isolating VLM performance on religious bias. However, in its qualitative and demonstrative examples, it showed that the evaluation framework successfully forces models to extract background knowledge regarding religious hate speech, such as correctly identifying Islamophobic stereotypes (e.g., labeling the portrayal of Muslims as 'sexually aggressive') as a mechanism of toxicity in targeted memes.
